A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same equivariant Hamiltonian-prediction network and augmented graph-partitioning approach, despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–I support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Hamiltonian-prediction experiments on amorphous materials, eigenvalue comparisons, ablations, perturbation analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original material-prediction experiments and reports additional device-transport simulations and small-molecule benchmark results.

M1.justification: The core architecture, orbital transformations, and augmented partitioning remain unchanged. V2 introduces an MD17-specific RMSE+MAE training criterion in Table 14, unlike v1's blanket MSE description in Appendix A. This is a limited reported objective adaptation, although v2 retains the generic MSE statement without reconciling the exception. Algorithm 1 documents the existing partitioning procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds transmission and electrical-current evaluation for TiN/a-HfOx/Ti/TiN devices with vacancy filaments under applied bias (Section 5), extending coverage beyond bulk Hamiltonians and eigenvalues. Its MD17 benchmark also adds uracil. Water and malondialdehyde were already evaluated in v1's message-passing-depth study, so their appearance is not entirely new coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an explicit comparison against QHNet for water, malondialdehyde, and uracil in Table 13. V1 cites the underlying work but provides no corresponding scored comparison against this network; its evaluated comparisons principally concern model/training variants and DFT references.

E3.justification: V2 extends the HfO2 cutoff sweep to 12 Å and changes PtGe's tested cutoffs from 6/8/16 Å to 4/6/8/10 Å. Appendix G reports 18 training slices instead of one, although Table 8's caption still says one. The new MD17 comparison specifies 200,000 training steps, revised splits, and different precision/model settings; its malondialdehyde and uracil validation counts differ between QHNet and the proposed model. Device evaluation introduces open boundaries and applied bias.

E4.justification: V1's one-versus-two message-passing-layer analysis (Figure 10) and one-versus-two training-structure study (Appendix I.1/Table 9) are removed. V2 revises the cutoff sensitivity studies and adds a transfer test from uniformly distributed vacancies to device structures containing vacancy filaments. The existing locality-perturbation and partition-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 11's runtime medians, standard-deviation bands, and measurements over the first 30 minutes of training. V2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests for prediction accuracy.

E6.justification: Numerical results change across Tables 2–5 and 10–12. At retained Table 4 settings, HfO2 at 8 Å changes from 5.16 to 4.84 meV, GST from 2.77 to 2.40 meV, and PtGe at 8 Å from 2.39 to 2.49 meV. Figure 5's all-state relative L1 error changes from 0.550% to 0.530%. V2 adds device and QHNet benchmark results. The replacement of PtGe's 16 Å result by a 10 Å result is not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The equivariance relations, coupled-basis transformation, and existing mathematical reasoning are retained. Abbreviating the Clebsch–Gordan coefficient as C is equivalent notation. V2 adds no substantive theorem, proof, or derivation; its partitioning pseudocode explains the existing procedure.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a local equivariant Hamiltonian network and accuracy-preserving augmented partitioning. The abstract tightens its reported eigenvalue-error bound from ≤1% to ≤0.53%, and the introduction replaces the 0.99–5.16 meV summary with 2.17–2.58 meV, reflecting the revised best-per-material results.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds substantive interpretation connecting vacancy-induced states and filament formation to electrical transport, and qualifies the usefulness of predicted Hamiltonians despite imperfect quantitative agreement. V2 removes v1's interpretations concerning diminishing benefits from additional message-passing layers in larger environments and gains from additional training structures. It also drops the claim that partitioning consistently reduces convergence epochs.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the anonymized code placeholder and future dataset-release promise with explicit code/data access locations. It adds partitioning pseudocode, MD17 splits and hyperparameters (Tables 13–14), and identifies ASE in PtGe generation. The amorphous-model hyperparameters remain unchanged. Some disclosure is lost, including the explicit 20,000-epoch cap previously stated for HfOx experiments.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the Tensor Field Networks attribution to Hodapp and Shapeev with Thomas et al. (2018), adds Miret et al. (2025) for device-scale motivation, and adds QUIP and ASE references. These are limited attribution and positioning changes; the broader relationship to existing equivariant Hamiltonian models remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main methodological organization are retained. V2 changes the title, makes localized explanatory edits, inserts the device-transport section and availability/acknowledgement statements, and revises Appendix I's subsections. These are limited structural and language revisions alongside the scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 adds device Figure 6/Table 6, MD17 Tables 13–14, and Algorithm 1, while removing v1 Figure 10 and Table 9. It rearranges Figure 2, revises Figure 3's schematic and output-head label, changes cutoff-table columns, and resizes or relocates retained figures. This substantially revises the displays beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The device-transport tests and explicit QHNet comparison strengthen validation, while access information and partitioning pseudocode improve reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removal of two informative ablations and unresolved reporting conflicts: one versus 18 slices in Appendix G/Table 8, and MSE versus RMSE+MAE in Appendix A/Table 14. The new device evidence is useful, but Section 5's claimed five-order current range also exceeds the approximately 3.3 orders shown in Table 6.
